# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteEth: MAC, PHYs and PTP core. It is generated
from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated on five configurations
without running an FPGA toolchain. The two `registers.py` configurations are designs
of the manual only, elaborated for this appendix: their clocks are placeholders and
they are not designs to build. Offsets are in bytes from the base of the bank; the
base addresses depend on the SoC and are in the `csr.csv` of a build. Every PHY bank is
named `ethphy` in a build; this appendix suffixes it with the PHY (`ethphy_basex`,
`ethphy_baser`) to keep the PHYs apart. The core layers (ARP, IP, ICMP, UDP), the
Etherbone and the UDP streamer have no registers.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `wishbone_mii` | `gen` `examples/wishbone_mii.yml` |
| `colorlight` | `bench/colorlight_5a_75b`  |
| `arty_10baset` | `bench/arty_10baset`  |
| `xcku3p_10g_ptp` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_xcku3p_10g_ptp` |
| `acorn_1000basex` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_acorn_1000basex` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The BIOS, Linux and the host tools use these
names through the generated `csr.h` and `csr.csv`.

## MAC {#reg-ethmac}

Defined by `LiteEthMAC` (`liteeth/mac/__init__.py`).

The bank of the MAC with SRAM slots (`interface="wishbone"` or `"hybrid"`), as
`add_ethernet`, `add_etherbone(with_ethmac=True)` and the `wishbone` and `axi-lite`
flavours of the generator build it. The `sram_writer_` registers describe the receive
slots and the `sram_reader_` registers the transmit slots; their events drive the
`ethmac` interrupt. The slots are memory in the `ethmac` bus region, not registers.
`rx_datapath_drops` exists when the MAC stores whole frames before forwarding them, as
the 64-bit MAC of `xcku3p_10g_ptp` does. `add_ethernet(with_timestamp=True)` adds
`sram_writer_timestamp`, `sram_reader_timestamp_slot` and `sram_reader_timestamp`.

Bank `ethmac`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `sram_writer_` `slot` | `0x0000` | 1 | ro | Receive slot. |
| `sram_writer_` `length` | `0x0004` | 11 | ro | Receive packet length in bytes. |
| `sram_writer_` `errors` | `0x0008` | 32 | ro | Receive packet drop count. |
| `sram_writer_ev_` `status` | `0x000c` | 1 | ro | This register contains the current raw level of the event trigger. Writes to this register have no effect. |
| `sram_writer_ev_` `pending` | `0x0010` | 1 | rw | When an event occurs, the corresponding bit will be set in this register. To clear the Event, set the corresponding bit in this register. |
| `sram_writer_ev_` `enable` | `0x0014` | 1 | rw | This register enables the corresponding events. Write a ``0`` to this register to disable individual events. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sram_reader_` `start` | `0x0018` | 1 | wo | Write strobe. |
| `sram_reader_` `ready` | `0x001c` | 1 | ro | Transmit command FIFO ready. |
| `sram_reader_` `level` | `0x0020` | 2 | ro | Transmit command FIFO level. |
| `sram_reader_` `slot` | `0x0024` | 1 | rw | Transmit slot. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sram_reader_` `length` | `0x0028` | 11 | rw | Transmit packet length in bytes. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sram_reader_ev_` `status` | `0x002c` | 1 | ro | This register contains the current raw level of the event trigger. Writes to this register have no effect. |
| `sram_reader_ev_` `pending` | `0x0030` | 1 | rw | When an event occurs, the corresponding bit will be set in this register. To clear the Event, set the corresponding bit in this register. |
| `sram_reader_ev_` `enable` | `0x0034` | 1 | rw | This register enables the corresponding events. Write a ``0`` to this register to disable individual events. Reset `0x0`. |
| `preamble_crc` | `0x0038` | 1 | ro | Preamble/CRC support enabled. |
| `rx_datapath_` `preamble_` `errors` | `0x003c` | 32 | ro | Preamble error count. |
| `rx_datapath_` `crc_errors` | `0x0040` | 32 | ro | CRC error count. |
| `rx_datapath_` `drops` | `0x0044` | 32 | ro | Receive packet drop count. |

## MII PHY {#reg-ethphy-mii}

Defined by `LiteEthPHYMII` (`liteeth/phy/parallel/mii.py`).

`crg_reset` holds the PHY, and the external PHY through its reset pin, in reset while
set. `mdio_w` and `mdio_r` drive the MDIO bus bit by bit; the BIOS commands
`mdio_read`, `mdio_write` and `mdio_dump` use them. The parallel PHYs whose pads have
an `mdc` signal have the same MDIO registers, as the ECP5 RGMII PHY shows.

Bank `ethphy_mii`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `crg_reset` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | PHY reset. Reset `0x0`. |
| `mdio_w` | `0x0004` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `mdio_r` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | MDIO read data. |

Fields of `mdio_w`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `mdc` | 0 | MDIO clock. |
| `oe` | 1 | MDIO output enable. |
| `w` | 2 | MDIO write data. |

## ECP5 RGMII PHY {#reg-ethphy-ecp5-rgmii}

Defined by `LiteEthECP5PHYRGMII` (`liteeth/phy/parallel/rgmii/ecp5.py`).

`rx_inband_status` decodes the in-band status that the external PHY sends between
frames: link, speed and duplex as the external PHY negotiated them.

Bank `ethphy_ecp5_rgmii`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `crg_reset` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | PHY reset. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_inband_` `status` | `0x0004` | 4 | ro | RGMII in-band status. |
| `mdio_w` | `0x0008` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `mdio_r` | `0x000c` | 1 | ro | MDIO read data. |

Fields of `rx_inband_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `link_status` | 0 | Link status. |
| `clock_speed` | 2:1 | Clock speed. |
| `duplex_status` | 3 | Duplex status. |

Fields of `mdio_w`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `mdc` | 0 | MDIO clock. |
| `oe` | 1 | MDIO output enable. |
| `w` | 2 | MDIO write data. |

## 10BASE-T PHY {#reg-ethphy-10baset}

Defined by `LiteEthPHY10BASET` (`liteeth/phy/serial/baset.py`).

`status` reports the link, detected from the frames and link pulses of the partner,
and whether the receive pair is wired inverted.

Bank `ethphy_10baset`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `status` | `0x0000` | 2 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `crg_reset` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | PHY reset. Reset `0x0`. |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `link_up` | 0 | Link up (frames/link pulses received). |
| `inverted` | 1 | Receive pair polarity inverted. |

## 1000BASE-X PHY {#reg-ethphy-basex}

Defined by `A7_1000BASEX` (`liteeth/phy/serial/basex/wrappers/a7_gtp.py`).

`reset` resets the transceiver and the PCS. `pcs_status` exists only when the PCS is
built with its registers, as here (`pcs_kwargs` with `with_csr`); the generator and the
bench targets build the BASE-X PHYs without it. The PCS also creates a link event,
which this wrapper does not export as registers.

Bank `ethphy_basex`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `pcs_status` | `0x0000` | 32 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `reset` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | PHY reset. Reset `0x0`. |

Fields of `pcs_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `link_up` | 0 | Link is up. |
| `is_sgmii` | 1 | SGMII in-use. |
| `config_reg` | 31:16 | Link partner ability register. |

## BASE-R PHY {#reg-ethphy-baser}

Defined by `LiteEthBASERPHY` (`liteeth/phy/serial/baser/wrappers/diagnostics.py`).

The same bank on the Artix-7, Kintex-7 and UltraScale+ BASE-R PHYs built with
`with_csr=True`. The GW5 10GBASE-R PHY adds `serdes_status`, ignores the `loopback`
field and has `rx_prbs_errors` only with `with_prbs=True`. Reading `status` clears its
sticky bits. [Debugging](#debugging) gives the read sequences.

Bank `ethphy_baser`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `reset` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | PHY reset. Reset `0x0`. |
| `control` | `0x0004` | 6 | rw | PHY control. Reset `0x0`. |
| `status` | `0x0008` | 13 | ro | PHY status. |
| `rx_prbs_errors` | `0x000c` | 32 | ro | PRBS31 bit errors since the test was last enabled, saturating rather than wrapping. Set prbs_pause and wait for prbs_paused before reading all words. Clear prbs_pause and wait for prbs_paused to clear before requesting another snapshot. Disabling the checker clears the counter, even while paused. For a bit error ratio, the denominator is the elapsed time times the receive clock frequency times 66 bits per block. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `loopback` | 2:0 | Transceiver loopback (UG578 ch 2): 0 off, 1 near-end PCS, 2 near-end PMA, 4 far-end PMA, 6 far-end PCS |
| `tx_prbs31_` `enable` | 3 | Transmit PRBS31 test pattern (49.2.8) |
| `rx_prbs31_` `enable` | 4 | Check received stream against PRBS31 (49.2.12) |
| `prbs_pause` | 5 | Freeze the PRBS31 error counter; wait for prbs_paused before reading |

Fields of `status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `block_lock` | 0 | Block synchronisation acquired (49.2.9, Figure 49-12) |
| `high_ber` | 1 | Invalid sync-header threshold exceeded in the rate-specific BER window |
| `link_up` | 2 | PCS_status: block lock held and no high BER (49.2.14.1) |
| `error_count` | 9:3 | PRBS31 bit errors in a sampled receive block, valid in receive test-pattern mode |
| `block_lock_lost` | 10 | Block lock has been absent at some point since this register was last read |
| `high_ber_` `latched` | 11 | high_ber has been asserted at some point since this register was last read |
| `prbs_paused` | 12 | The paused PRBS31 counter snapshot has reached sys; zero without PRBS support |

## PTP {#reg-ptp}

Defined by `LiteEthPTP` (`liteeth/core/ptp/__init__.py`).

Two status registers only: the enable, mode, clock identity, time and servo state of
the PTP core are gateware signals for the user logic.

Bank `ptp`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `locked` | `0x0000` | 1 | ro | PTP lock status. |
| `master_ip` | `0x0004` | 32 | ro | Master IPv4. |
